description.en: MetroLLM-Bench evaluates language models as transit kiosk policy layers across six real metro systems. It includes 955 cases covering routing, fare calculation, disruptions, accessibility, and adversarial input, with models required to call structured tools and submit machine-renderable terminal states.

attentionForecast.reason: The benchmark targets a concrete, broadly understandable real-world application with released code, models, and a live demo, likely generating interest from both applied ML practitioners and transit system developers.

curation.decisionReason: The benchmark is formally named in the paper title, includes detailed task definitions, deterministic Tier 1 and LLM-judged Tier 2 scoring, and a public GitHub release with harness, reproduction guide, and models.

evaluationEvidence.reuse: The benchmark, harness, reproduction guide, and fine-tuned students are released at https://github.com/continker/metrollm-bench.
evaluationEvidence.scoring: Fourteen deterministic scoring components form Tier 1; eight semantic-quality components form Tier 2, six of which use a language-model judge. We report Tier 1 and the combined score of both tiers.
evaluationEvidence.task: It is a 955-case benchmark across six metro systems. Each case asks whether a language model can run a transit kiosk from a prose prompt, handling routing, fares, and disruptions through tool calls, with no code changes.
